title: C4OS Grill Question 039 - Plugin Marketplace And Lifecycle

questions.label: Which Codex marketplace sources should C4OS support?
questions.help: Recommended: mirror Codex's marketplace model: bundled/default, repo, personal, local marketplace root, GitHub shorthand, Git URL, ref, and sparse paths.
options: Bundled/default, repo, personal, local root, GitHub, Git URL, ref, and sparse paths
Bundled/default, repo, and personal marketplaces only
Bundled/default and local marketplace roots only
Any filesystem path only; no marketplace catalog model
Other

questions.label: Should built-in C4OS plugins be modeled as a bundled marketplace source?
questions.help: Recommended: model built-ins as a bundled/default marketplace source so install, uninstall, reinstall, and source display follow the same catalog lifecycle.
options: Yes; built-ins are a bundled/default marketplace source
No; built-ins are separate app-bundle plugin roots
Yes, but hide the marketplace source from normal UI
Other

questions.label: Where should installed plugin bundles live?
questions.help: Recommended: C4OS-owned user config/cache path that mirrors Codex cache semantics without writing into ~/.codex as C4OS state.
options: C4OS-owned cache path mirroring Codex cache semantics
Use the Codex ~/.codex/plugins/cache path directly
Load directly from marketplace source paths without cache copy
Plugin source decides
Other

questions.label: After uninstall, how should reinstall work?
questions.help: Recommended: uninstall removes the installed cache copy and enabled state; reinstall resolves again from the marketplace source.
options: Remove installed cache copy; reinstall from marketplace source
Keep installed cache copy hidden; reinstall restores it
Delete source files too when local
Uninstall only disables plugins
Other

questions.label: When should plugin lifecycle changes require restart?
questions.help: Codex docs mention restart after local marketplace changes and config disablement. C4OS can still decide whether shell-only changes can apply live.
options: Live for UI/settings; restart required for native backend registration changes
Follow Codex-style restart for install, uninstall, enable, and disable
All plugin lifecycle changes require restart
Plugin manifest decides whether restart is required
Other

questions.label: What happens to plugin-owned user data when a plugin is uninstalled?
questions.help: Recommended: keep plugin-owned data by default and offer a separate remove-data action so uninstall is reversible and does not destroy chats or plugin records accidentally.
options: Keep plugin-owned data; separate remove-data action
Prompt during uninstall whether to delete data
Always delete plugin-owned data
Plugin manifest decides
Other

questions.label: Notes or corrections
questions.help: Clarify marketplace source trust, installed cache semantics, source refresh, update checks, reinstall UX, restart prompts, or data deletion semantics.
